title: Prometheus & Grafana upgrade playbook for bare‑metal/private VPC
content:
Scope and intent:

This note captures a pragmatic, low-risk playbook for upgrading Prometheus/Grafana and OTEL collector deployments running in customer VPCs and on-prem racks (bare‑metal). The audience is platform engineers and SREs who operate Redwood Private observability stacks or support customer migrations. The guidance is purposely conservative: aim for zero-data-loss for metrics and logs, keep alerting sane during cutover, and minimize blast radius.

High-level approach:

- Non-destructive, canary-first upgrades: introduce new components alongside existing ones, validate, then switch traffic.
- Use Terraform modules and feature-flagged rollouts for infra changes so we can reliably roll back.
- Separate control-plane changes (Config, dashboards, provisioning) from data-plane changes (collectors, remote_write endpoints).
- Prioritize metrics continuity (Prometheus scrape targets + remote_write) before changing retention/backends.

Key constraints and assumptions:

- Some deployments are air-gapped—assume limited internet egress.
- Disk is constrained on older nodes; avoid large retention increases during migration.
- Running Prometheus instances are currently serverful (systemd pods/containers) or k8s StatefulSets depending on customer.
- Grafana is provisioned via provisioning files in a shared git repo for most customers, but some use manual dashboards.

Pre-upgrade checklist (operator):

- Verify backups exist: snapshot Prometheus TSDB (promtool snapshots) and export Grafana dashboards via API.
- Confirm Terraform state is up to date and locked. Capture current module versions.
- Healthcheck: all scrape targets up for 24h, alerting flaps resolved, disk usage <75% on TSDB nodes.
- Identify high-risk alerts and temporarily route to a muted channel during migration window.
- Ensure log shipping pipeline has store-and-forward capability where possible (e.g., Fluent Bit with local buffer) in case of temporary downstream outage.

Phased plan (details):

Phase A — Prep & small canary (parallel install)
- Deploy a new OTEL collector pair (or deployment) in the same network with a label like telemetry-canary-otel. Configure the collector to speak to new downstream endpoints (Temporarily: remote_write to a dedicated canary Cortex/Thanos write path and logs to a canary S3/bucket).
- Provision an additional Prometheus instance (prom-canary) with a reduced scrape set for critical services only (api, gateway, inference). Use the same scrape configs as prod but limit targets to 10–20% to reduce load.
- Provision Grafana read-only instance (grafana-canary) with subset of dashboards.
- Validate end-to-end: collector->remote_write and prom-canary scapes and ingestion visible in canary Grafana.
- Observe for 48 hours to capture typical traffic patterns.

Phase B — Terraform module notes & infra changes
- Keep modules idempotent: split module into "prometheus-core" and "prometheus-remote" so remote_write backends can be toggled independently.
- Module variables to add:
  - enable_remote_write (bool)
  - remote_write_endpoint_list (list of strings)
  - remote_write_tls (bool)
  - prometheus_retention_override (string)
  - tsdb_node_count (int)
- For bare-metal deployments, provide an option to set systemd unit drop-in config via module for resource limits (CPU quota, IO niceness).
- Add lifecycle prevent_destroy on critical PVC resources during first two deploys as safety.
- Use terraform apply with -target to only apply collector/prometheus canary resources in initial step.

Phase C — Canary expansion and dual-write
- Enable dual-write: configure the old Prometheus to continue local writes while the new remote_write pipeline accepts traffic from newly deployed collectors and prom-canary.
- For collectors, enable batching and a healthy retry/backoff to avoid transient spikes on downstream.
- Compare series counts, label cardinality, and cardinality deltas between old and new paths. Flag anomalies >10% cardinality difference for manual review.

Phase D — Controlled cutover
- Increase scrape coverage on prom-canary to full set, still in parallel with existing Prometheus for 6–12 hours.
- Once parity confirmed (series counts, basic query latencies), flip routing at the service discovery layer: point service discovery (Consul/K8s endpoints/Terraform provisioned DNS) at new collectors/prometheus pool first for non-critical routes.
- Run a smoke runbook: run queries for 30 representative MQL/PromQL queries and record times/values.

Phase E — Decommission and cleanup
- Keep old Prometheus instances running read-only for at least 7 days to allow on-demand historical queries. Mark them in Grafana as "legacy-archive".
- Rotate TLS certs if new endpoints used different certs; ensure certs are stored in KMS/HSM where applicable.
- Remove prevent_destroy flags and then scale down old resources.

Operational details and gotchas:

- TSDB snapshots: promtool snapshot produces a directory that must be securely copied to long-term object store. For very large TSDBs (>1TB), plan a dedicated transfer window.
- WAL corruption: When copying tsdb, ensure Prometheus is stopped cleanly to avoid WAL corruption. If not possible, use the snapshot API.
- Disk pressure: If retention must temporarily be reduced to avoid OOM, do so before cutover and document the retention revert.
- Label cardinality: New collectors with OTEL instrumentation may add extra labels (service.instance, host.id). Add relabel_configs to strip unnecessary high-cardinality labels before storing.

Grafana provisioning approach:

- Use provisioning files in git for datasources and folder/dashboard provisioning. Keep a canary provisioning directory and a CI job that validates dashboard JSON schemas before apply.
- During migration, add a readonly datasource alias "prom_remote" that points to the new backend; do not remove existing datasources until after the read-only window.

OTEL collector specifics:

- Recommended receiver config: prometheus receiver (for scraping), jaeger/zipkin if tracing, and fluentforward for logs if present.
- Exporters: remote_write (prometheusremotewrite) and OTLP for metrics/logs to the new backend. For air-gapped, use filesystem exporter as intermediate buffer.
- Memory tuning: use memory_limiter processor with 25% of container memory as limit and 10% spike buffer.

Terraform snippets (illustrative) — include as text only:

# module usage example
module "prometheus_core" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//prometheus-core?ref=v1.3.0"
  prometheus_retention_override = var.prometheus_retention_override
  tsdb_node_count = var.tsdb_node_count
  enable_remote_write = false
}

module "otel_canary" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//otel-collector?ref=v0.9.2"
  name = "otel-canary"
  config_s3_key = var.otel_canary_config_key
  remote_write_endpoint_list = [var.canary_remote_write_endpoint]
}

Rollback plan:

- If canary shows anomalies or new backend rejects >0.5% of writes: immediately disable remote_write in collector config via terraform and revert Prometheus service discovery to old endpoints.
- For Grafana anomalies, re-point dashboards to legacy datasource and revert provisioning commit.
- Keep old nodes intact until confirmation window passes.

Testing and validation checklist:

- Canary ingestion rate within +/-15% of expected for 48 hours.
- No sustained increase in dropped series or write errors.
- Alerting smoke test: trigger synthetic alert and verify upstream routing.
- Query parity checks for 20 golden queries.

Post-upgrade monitoring and follow-up:

- Keep increased retention of ingestion metrics for 14 days in the control plane (to monitor subtle regressions).
- Run a postmortem if any customer-facing incidents occur during migration window.
- Capture Terraform plan artifacts and a short runbook describing the exact steps taken (apply commands, targets, time windows).

Appendix — quick reference: terraform flags and safe commands

- terraform plan -out plan.tfplan
- terraform apply plan.tfplan
- terraform apply -target=module.otel_canary -auto-approve (use sparingly)
- git tag the provision changes (grafana-provisioning-canary) and attach the tag to the rollout ticket

Notes to self / open questions:

- Need a small utility that diffs label cardinality across two Prometheus backends and outputs a simple report (series count by metric and top label keys).
- Confirm whether any customers depend on Prometheus local write semantics for edge workflows; those may require special migration adapters.

End.
